title: Staple price patterns across WFP-reporting countries, 2017-2026
question: How did retail cereal and tuber prices trend, how volatile were they month to month, how strong was their seasonal cycle and how closely did markets move together, country by country?
hypothesis: None tested. A descriptive inventory to show where seasonality and volatility are large enough for forecasting questions to matter.
estimand: Per commodity group: median across series of the log-linear trend (% per year), the standard deviation of month-on-month log changes between consecutive observed months, the seasonal amplitude of detrended log prices, and the mean pairwise correlation of monthly log changes.

population.selection_rule: per country, the commodity groups with the most eligible series (ties by commodity code); eligibility is computed from metadata only (counts, coverage, gaps), never from model performance

timing.vintage_statement: Backtests use today's revised data; original publication dates are not available from the providers, so information timing is an explicitly assumed release lag, not an observed real-time vintage.

inference.unit_of_inference: forecast-origin month: losses are averaged within each month before testing, so thousands of market-month forecasts are not treated as independent observations

limitations: Nominal local-currency prices; trends include general inflation and currency depreciation, so they are not comparable across countries as real price changes.
Seasonal amplitude needs at least 36 observed months per series; shorter series contribute trend and volatility only.
Group medians summarise markets with different reporting intensity; they are not national averages.
